messages:
jamie: FYI — saw a big uptick in GPU pod evictions in SFO around 03:12 UTC, traffic auto-shifted to euc1 and we hit tail latencies for several customers. Opening a thread for post-incident action items and runbook changes.

devon: digging into node logs now. early signs: CNI flaps + kube-scheduler pressure on the SFO AZ. eviction storms started after burst allocations from a few noisy tenants. reserve pool didn't replenish quickly enough.

sarah: confirmed — reserve-pool autoscaler lagged. we have a short window where burst demand > warm-pool capacity and the eviction threshold (pod_ready < 0.55) kicked in too aggressively.

maria: TL;DR impact: ~8% increased 99p latency for hostnames routed to euc1, a few user sessions timed out. no data loss. customer-facing incidents page updated.

liam: cost note — the emergency shift and extra burst in euc1 incurred ~12% extra GPU-hours for the day. we should estimate recurring risk if we loosen thresholds.

oncall-bot: Incident: region-ejection-sfo-03:12 — severity: mitigated — auto-shift executed to euc1 at 03:14 UTC — lead: devon.

ryan: quick replay steps that helped: 1) temporarily capped incoming trafficslice for SFO via the traffic-sherpa UI, 2) forced reserve-pool scale-up, 3) paused background batch jobs on noisy customers.

jamie: propose runbook changes: a) add "eviction smoothing": require N consecutive eviction signals before global shift, b) tiered reserve-pool pre-warm for known heavy tenants, c) add a short cooldown for auto-shift weighting to avoid oscillation.

sarah: agree. also add explicit telemetry alerts for reserve-pool fill-rate and for scheduler queue backlog so ops knows before evictions start.

devon: small config snippet I'd like in the runbook (for ops use):
```
# enforce smoothing: require 3 eviction events across >2 AZs within 5m before auto-shift
redwood policy set eviction_smoothing --threshold 3 --window 300
# shift CLI (temporary manual):
redwood shift --from sfo --to euc1 --weight 0.2 --cooldown 600
```

maria: can we add a checklist item to try a weighted, gradual shift instead of full cutover? that reduced user impact during the incident. call it "weighted cool-shift" in the playbook.

liam: putting a finance guardrail: if emergency shift > 10 GPU-hours in a rolling 24h, send an alert to finance and mark for invoice review. don't block the shift but flag it.

jamie: good. also: update the reserve-pool autoscaler config to respect tenant tagging priority. high-priority customers should get fast pre-warm lanes.

devon: action items (initial):
- devon: PR runbook edits with eviction_smoothing + cool-shift examples — due 2026-04-02
- sarah: telemetry alerts + dashboard widgets for reserve-pool fill-rate & scheduler backlog — due 2026-03-30
- liam: cost guardrail alert + billing tag flow — due 2026-03-28
- maria: add post-incident note to customer-facing incidents page & comms draft — due 2026-03-19
- jamie: add e2e dry-run playbook and a runthrough doc for oncall rotations — due 2026-04-06

oncall-bot: Created incident follow-up ticket: INC-2026-3121 (linked in playbook).

ryan: I opened a draft PR for the runbook here: https://git.redwood.dev/inference/runbooks/pull/482 — please comment. includes the smoothing thresholds and sample CLI commands.

sarah: will also add synthetic alerts (canaries) to validate reserve-pool replenish time after scale actions. want to run a canary next Tuesday in the staging region.

devon: one more operational tweak: increase kube-scheduler leader-election timeout in SFO by 30s to reduce churn after brief CNI blips. I'll add the kube manifest diff to the PR.

jamie: nice. let's also add a short runbook blurb on graceful drain vs immediate eviction when adjusting weights: prefer staged drain with 10% increments every 2 minutes for production slices.

maria: ack, adding to comms. linking to playbook PR in the customer note.

liam: finance ack, I'll wire up the alert and add an example report generation query for the next ops review.

jamie: final ask — assign a reviewer for the runbook PR (need infra + SRE sign-off). devon, can you request an SRE review?

devon: will do. pinging @sre-team for review in the PR and scheduling a 30m walkthrough tomorrow.

ryan: thanks everyone — this thread captured the steps I'll merge once PR feedback is in. adding :white_check_mark: for action owners.

jamie: closing the thread after actions are in backlog. follow-ups will live in INC-2026-3121 and the runbook PR. good work. :tada:
